tema: Past Simple Narrative — Tell Me a Story

cast_dialogue.linea: A trip becomes a legend when you tell it in order: first, then, next, finally. Narrate your adventure, heroes!
First, I packed my bag. Then I caught the train to the coast. Next, I arrived at the hotel... and suddenly, it started to rain!
Oh no! What did you do then?
Great story! First you packed, then you travelled, and finally you took photos — a perfect narrative!
Luckily, I met a friendly woman who lent me an umbrella. Finally, the sun came out and I took amazing photos.
That reminds me of my first trip to the sea. I got lost, but a fisherman showed me the way. Those were adventures!

Finally, the sun came out and I took photos.

Did you try the local food?
Did you have a good time? Yes, I did.
Did it rain? Yes, it did.
Did you get lost? No, I didn't.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: To tell a story in the past, chain events with sequencers: first, then, next, after that, finally. Add drama with 'suddenly' and relief with 'luckily'. All main verbs go in the past simple.

ejercicios.afirmacion: In a past narrative, all main verbs go in the past simple.
'Luckily' introduces a problem in the story.

guion: Ben: Tell me about your trip, Sofía!
Sofía: Well, first I packed my bag and caught the train.
Sofía: Then I arrived at the hotel. Suddenly, it started to rain!
Ben: Oh no! What happened next?
Sofía: Luckily, a woman lent me an umbrella. Finally, the sun came out and I took amazing photos.

reading.texto: Sofía's trip was a real adventure. First, she packed her bag and caught the train to the coast. Then she arrived at the hotel and left her things. Suddenly, it started to rain! Luckily, a friendly woman lent her an umbrella. After that, she tried the local food and bought some souvenirs. Finally, the sun came out, and she took amazing photos. She came back home tired but very happy.
